title: Mirror-image rule and counteroffers
summary: The traditional approach treats a qualified acceptance as rejection and a new offer, subject to interpretation of the actual response.
notes: Ardente makes the buyer’s request about furnishings a condition. The notes contrast terms already implied in the offer and unqualified acceptance accompanied by a merely precatory request. State v. Rios distinguishes inquiry about a better offer from rejection of the existing one. Different language does not mechanically mean a counteroffer; ask whether the response makes agreement dependent on the proposed change.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 269–272. Open assigned page 269.
